sasha: FYI onboarding sample fails to get proper generics in the edge ESM bundle. Runtime works but TS inference falls back to `any` for the SDK call generics.

marco: can you share tsconfig? often `moduleResolution`/`module` mismatch causes different overload resolution.

sasha: project uses `module: \"esnext\"`, `moduleResolution: \"bundler\"`, `esModuleInterop: false`. Repro: private repo. Minimal failure is an overload choosing a non-generic signature, collapsing `T` to `any`.

emily: paste the simplified signatures please.

sasha: here:
```ts
export function call<T>(route: string, opts?: CallOpts): Promise<T>
export function call(route: string, opts?: CallOpts): Promise<any>
```
Consumer ends up with `Promise<any>` even when they call `call<MyType>(...)`.

kevin: we saw this before: our build-time auth/retry wrapper becomes a `const call = createCall(auth)` which loses `declare function` semantics in emitted d.ts, making the compiler prefer the non-generic overload. The bundler dts emitter can reorder overloads.

emily: quick mitigations: (1) ship a preserved types file for ESM that uses `declare function call<T>(...)` before wrappers are applied, (2) add a compile-time CI job that runs `tsc --noEmit` across a matrix (`moduleResolution: bundler` and `node16`), (3) update onboarding docs with a recommended tsconfig snippet for edge targets.

marco: long-term we should refactor to a single generic signature with discriminated options instead of two overloads. Also try `declare function` + `export { call }` to keep overloads during emit. I'll pick up a ticket.

sasha: added repro and failing tsc command to the new ticket. note: `skipLibCheck` is not a real fix, it just hides the type regression for consumers.

devex-bot: Created ticket INF-8421: \"edge ESM d.ts overloads -> any inference\" assignee: @marco priority: P2 :thumbsup:
